note.body:
Hi Michael,

We're excited to welcome Rachel Steinberg to the team as the new VP Engineering, starting in 14 days on 2026-06-28.

The intro meeting has been scheduled for 2026-06-29 at 8:30 AM. This will be a great opportunity for you both to connect.

For the onboarding buddy, I'd suggest Helena Friedman. With her 3.4 years at the company and alignment in product strategy, she'll be beneficial for Rachel's transition.

Attached below is a draft of Rachel's 30-60-90 day plan. Please review and adjust it to fit your onboarding approach—it’s a starting point for your customization.

Additionally, you’ll find a manager prep checklist to ensure everything is ready for her first day.

Best regards,

The Onboarding team

thirty_days: Meet with key stakeholders across engineering, product, and leadership teams.
Review the current strategic initiatives and engineering projects in Notion and Slack.
Participate in board meetings or review board-docs to understand the current company outlook.
Conduct 1:1 meetings with direct reports to understand team dynamics.
sixty_days: Develop an actionable plan to address any gaps or opportunities noted in the first 30 days.
Initiate a small cross-functional project to drive collaboration within the team.
Report on progress and initial learnings in a leadership team meeting.
ninety_days: Present a strategic vision for the engineering department to the executive team.
Deliver a key initiative that aligns with company goals.
Establish a benchmark for future engineering projects and performance.

manager_checklist: Review Rachel's resume and cover letter for context on past achievements.
Prepare an introductory email to the team, announcing Rachel's role and start date.
Schedule a 1:1 meeting during Rachel's first week to discuss her onboarding experience and expectations.
Ensure all IT equipment and system accesses are ready for her first day.
Familiarize yourself with Rachel’s onboarding buddy to align on key onboarding priorities.
Prepare a list of key stakeholders for Rachel to meet in her first month.

We can’t wait to see the amazing things you’ll accomplish with us!

Best,

The Team

note.body:
Hi Michael,

We're excited to welcome Rachel Steinberg to the team as the new VP Engineering, starting in 14 days on 2026-06-28.

The intro meeting has been scheduled for 2026-06-29 at 8:30 AM. This will be a great opportunity for you both to connect.

For the onboarding buddy, I'd suggest Helena Friedman. With her 3.4 years at the company and alignment in product strategy, she'll be beneficial for Rachel's transition.

Attached below is a draft of Rachel's 30-60-90 day plan. Please review and adjust it to fit your onboarding approach—it’s a starting point for your customization.

Additionally, you’ll find a manager prep checklist to ensure everything is ready for her first day.

Best regards,

The Onboarding team

thirty_days: Meet with key stakeholders across engineering, product, and leadership teams.
Review the current strategic initiatives and engineering projects in Notion and Slack.
Participate in board meetings or review board-docs to understand the current company outlook.
Conduct 1:1 meetings with direct reports to understand team dynamics.
sixty_days: Develop an actionable plan to address any gaps or opportunities noted in the first 30 days.
Initiate a small cross-functional project to drive collaboration within the team.
Report on progress and initial learnings in a leadership team meeting.
ninety_days: Present a strategic vision for the engineering department to the executive team.
Deliver a key initiative that aligns with company goals.
Establish a benchmark for future engineering projects and performance.

manager_checklist: Review Rachel's resume and cover letter for context on past achievements.
Prepare an introductory email to the team, announcing Rachel's role and start date.
Schedule a 1:1 meeting during Rachel's first week to discuss her onboarding experience and expectations.
Ensure all IT equipment and system accesses are ready for her first day.
Familiarize yourself with Rachel’s onboarding buddy to align on key onboarding priorities.
Prepare a list of key stakeholders for Rachel to meet in her first month.

Hi Rachel,

We're thrilled to welcome you as our new VP of Engineering! The entire engineering leadership team is excited to have you join us here in San Francisco.

On your first day, you'll find your new MacBook Pro 16-inch all set up and ready to help you dive into the exciting work ahead. Helena Friedman, your onboarding buddy, will be there to guide you and make sure you feel right at home. Plus, you'll kick things off with an intro meeting with Michael Park at 8:30 AM to get a firsthand look at how we roll.

We can’t wait to see the amazing things you’ll accomplish with us!

Best,

The Team
